messages:
maya: Quick q — embeddings endpoint behavior for mixed inputs + long text? If a batch contains ["short", null, "" , <very long string>], do we truncate each item individually or drop items? Need to know how indices map to vectors.

jon: We truncate per-item, not per-batch. Each input corresponds to one vector in the same order. We do not drop entries unless they fail validation. Right now truncation uses EMBED_MAX_CHARS (4k) on the server.

priyanka: FYI we changed the empty/null handling last sprint: empty string returns a zero vector (all zeros) to preserve shape, null still returns 400 if the client sends explicit nulls in the array. That was to avoid shifting indices for downstream consumers. Might be worth revisiting.

maya: Thanks. Is that behavior documented in the spec? I couldn't find a clear line about null vs empty. Also how does truncation interact with multibyte unicode? We had a bug where emoji caused off-bytes and final vector mismatches.

sam: Good catch. Truncation is done by char count (UTF-8 code points) but the implementation used byte slicing. There's an open PR to switch to rune-aware truncation — see PR #4821. I'll add a note about emoji.

maya: Example payload I was testing:

```
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-001",
  "inputs": ["hello", null, "", "这是一个很长的文本... (repeat 1000x)"]
}
```

What should the response shape look like?

jon: Response should be an object with data: an array of embeddings in the same order as inputs. For empty string we return an embedding vector (0s). For null we return an error for the whole request currently (400) — but that's the part we debated.

priyanka: To be concrete:
- inputs length N -> data length N (unless request rejected)
- each data[i] -> { "embedding": [float,...], "index": i }
- embedding dims currently 1536 for redwood-embed-001

maya: OK that helps. Two follow-ups: 1) can we opt to make null -> preserve placeholder like {embedding: null, index: i} with 207 or 206 code instead of failing whole request? 2) batch size limit — what's max items per request?

sam: Current config allows up to 4096 items per request but we throttle by tokens and total payload size. We previously had users accidentally sending 100k tiny items and OOM'd a worker. Suggest adding per-request hard cap to 10k tokens and 8k items.

jon: On null behavior — we discussed a non-breaking approach: accept nulls and return {embedding: null, index: i} with overall 200 and a top-level warnings array. That keeps order and avoids breaking consumers. Need spec + implementation + tests.

priyanka: I'll draft the spec change and include examples (empty->zero vector, null->null placeholder). Also will add unicode-aware truncation note and vector dim.

sam: I'll pick up the PR for rune-aware truncation and add a guard for per-item byte size so we don't accidentally exceed kernel buffer limits.

infra-bot: deploy bot: patch-embed-null-handling merged to staging at 2026-03-18T09:12:03Z :shipit:

maya: Great. Action items summarized?

jon: Action items:
- priyanka: update API spec + migration note (embed null/empty semantics)
- sam: finish rune-aware trunc PR + add per-item guard + tests
- jon: add unit/integration tests that assert data length == inputs length and null placeholders preserved
- maya: add a short note in ops runbook about kernel buffer guard and failure observation

maya: I'll follow up tomorrow with links to the spec draft and test matrix. Thanks all :thumbsup:
